what is the total number of explicitly labeled ticks across all axes?
you should write down the labels from top to bottom, then from left to right and separate the labels with commas
your final answer should account for only labels relevant to the plot in the legend, even if the legend is located outside the plot
your final answer should be the most relevant title of the plot that is explicitly written
your final answer should be the number of lines in the plot. ignore grid lines, tick marks, and any vertical or horizontal auxiliary lines
your final answer should be the total number of explicitly labeled ticks across all axes, including the case when any axis is shared across multiple subplots
your final answer should be within a few words, such as increases, increases then stabilizes
your final answer should be yes if any lines intersect, and no otherwise
your final answer should follow n by m format, where n is the number of rows and m is the number of columns
give a score of 1 if and only if the extracted answer and the ground truth answer are referring to the same term
when ground truth answer is not applicable, the response must express not applicable to receive a score of 1

info. extr.=information extraction, enum.=enumeration, patt. rec.=pattern recognition, cntg.=counting, comp.=compositionality
models with (*) are those whose performance is constrained by input resolutions
charxiv consists of 2,323 charts paired with more than 10k questions
we randomly sample 1,000 charts as the validation set and use the rest as the test set
we release all qa pairs for the validation set and keep the answers to the test set private to prevent data leakage
existing datasets often focus on oversimplified and homogeneous charts with template-based questions, leading to an over-optimistic measure of progress
more complex reasoning questions from mmc cannot be solved from the charts alone and require external domain-specific knowledge (e.g., mapping acronyms in the legend to particular algorithms)
all figures were re-rendered into high-resolution jpeg format, with the longer side of each figure resized to 1024px
at the end of this four-step pipeline, we have 2,323 charts in total
most figures in arxiv source files are diagrams, illustrations, and natural images, not charts
we downloaded all arxiv preprints on eight academic subjects from january 2020 to september 2023
we randomly sample 750 candidate figures from the pre-filtered set for each subject and year
we remove the charts that exhibit large (≥ 0.95) pairwise cosine similarities with the other candidates
we utilize a pretrained siglip visual encoder [67] to identify candidate figures that exhibit a cosine similarity of at least 0.65 with the average image embedding of existing charts from mathvista
these questions are broadly categorized into five groups: information extraction, enumeration, pattern recognition, counting, and compositionality
we designed a total of 19 templates for descriptive questions
we pair each chart with four descriptive questions and one of them is intentionally designed to be unanswerable
we construct the query by prepending the subplot prefix (e.g., for the subplot at row m and column n) before the question when there are multiple subplots
we opt out of exact match and instead use gpt-4o [1] to extract the answer and assign binary scores based on the correctness

we evaluate a diverse set of general-purpose multimodal large language models (mllms) that can (1) process input resolution greater or equal to 448 × 448 and (2) achieve a score of at least 36 on the testmini set of mathvista
the leading proprietary model, gpt-4o, exhibits strong capabilities in answering descriptive questions, lagging just 7.65% behind human performance
the top-performing open source model internvl chat v1.5 exhibits a 25.95% drop in performance compared to gpt-4o
human accuracy is only 80.5% and 92.1% in reasoning and descriptive questions
we hypothesize that this could be due to issues with automated grading or mistakes by participants in the human evaluation study

CharXiv has been officially adopted into frontier model evaluations for GPT-4.1, Qwen2.5-VL, InternVL2.5, Doubao-1.5-pro, and more!
CharXiv is accepted at NeurIPS 2024 Datasets & Benchmarks Track and NeurIPS 2024 Multimodal Algorithmic Reasoning Workshop as a spotlight paper
We released the full evaluation pipeline (i.e., v1.0).
We updated the leaderboard with the latest models: o1, Qwen2-VL, Pixtral, InternVL 2.5, Llama 3.2 Vision, NVLM, Molmo, Llava OneVision, Phi 3.5, and more!
Note that all models are evaluated in a zero-shot setting with a set of natural instructions for each question type.
The numbers below are based on the model performance on the validation set, which consists of 1,000 charts and 5,000 questions in total.
a comprehensive evaluation suite involving 2,323 natural, challenging, and diverse charts from scientific papers
all charts and questions are handpicked, curated, and verified by human experts
descriptive questions about examining basic chart elements
reasoning questions that require synthesizing information across complex visual elements in the chart
